Scope: Crime prevention and policing interventions, field experiments, implementation studies and evaluations involving prefectural police forces, the National Police Agency, the National Research Institute of Police Science, the National Police Academy and other police bodies working with university researchers and other research partners.
Inclusion policy: Studies are not selected on the basis of research-design strength or whether results are statistically significant. Observational and policy-development studies are also retained where they contribute to understanding a broader intervention or research programme.
Additional sources: University bulletins and institutional repositories, official police research reports, reports from public and research organisations such as the Nikkoso Research Foundation for Safe Society, conference abstracts and ongoing research projects.
Publication types: Peer-reviewed articles, university bulletins, conference abstracts, official reports, press materials and ongoing research are recorded separately. 'Peer-reviewed' does not by itself mean that the evidence is strong.
Duplicate records: Where a conference presentation and a later journal article represent separate publications from the same underlying study, they are generally retained as separate records. The priority is to make the development of research programmes traceable.
Limitations: This is an initial database designed to maximise coverage. Additional material is likely to remain in local university bulletins, internal police publications and conference proceedings that are not fully indexed online.
Main search sources: J-STAGE, CiNii Research, university institutional repositories, official websites of the National Police Agency and prefectural police forces, KAKEN, the Nikkoso Research Foundation for Safe Society, and university researcher databases.
Nikkoso Research Foundation for Safe Soc: Post-2010 research reports on public safety and crime prevention are reviewed separately. The core database prioritises material directly connected to police–researcher collaboration, interventions and evaluation.
Regularly searched conference sources: Annual meeting abstracts, proceedings and conference papers from the Japanese Association of Criminal Psychology, Japanese Association of Sociological Criminology, Association of Behavioral Economics and Finance, Japanese Society of Social Psychology, Japanese Psychological Association, Behaviormetric Society of Japan, Japanese Society of Environmental Psychology, Man-Environment Research Association and GIS Association of Japan.
Treatment of conference abstracts: Searches cover not only conference programmes but also publicly available abstracts, proceedings, J-STAGE, CiNii Research and J-GLOBAL. A conference paper and a later publication are retained as separate records where they are distinct documents. Where police involvement or methods cannot be confirmed, details are not inferred and the item is flagged for further verification.
